summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, a history of kidney transplantation, and recurrent urinary tract infections was admitted with nausea, vomiting, fatigue, and low-grade fever. Initial evaluation revealed leukocytosis, elevated creatinine, and urinalysis consistent with infection. She was started on IV ceftriaxone, but urine culture identified multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae resistant to ceftriaxone. Treatment was switched to meropenem, and a midline was placed to complete a 14-day course of IV ertapenem as an outpatient. She remained afebrile, with improving renal function and white blood cell count. Her diabetes was managed with her insulin pump, and she was counseled on tighter glycemic control and vaginal estrogen to reduce future infection risk. She was discharged home with visiting nurse support for antibiotic infusions and follow-up plans with her transplant and infectious disease teams.
problems: Renal tubulo-interstitial disorders in diseases classified elsewhere
